newsitem.title: USA: Packwood will not rule out future bid for office.
newsitem.headline: Packwood will not rule out future bid for office.

text.p: Former Sen. Bob Packwood, who resigned in 1995 amid a sexual misconduct scandal, said Thursday he would not rule out the possibility of running for public office again in the future.
"You never want to say never," he told Reuters before a luncheon speech. "You don't want to foreclose any doors in life."
Asked whether he would consider running for federal or state office, Packwood replied: "I haven't even approached that bridge, let alone crossing it."

Packwood, 64, a moderate Republican who served 26 years in the Senate, held on to his seat tenaciously through more than two years of revelations about his sexual conduct from former staff members and associates that first surfaced shortly after he was elected to a fifth term in 1992.
He finally stepped down after the Ethics Committee unanimously recommended his expulsion, in part because he allegedly altered diaries submitted as evidence in the case.

Since leaving the Senate more than 16 months ago, Packwood has worked in Washington as an independent consultant on trade and tax issues, and he said the business is doing well enough that he is considering hiring a staff.
Seemingly relaxed, Packwood said he had lost weight and was playing squash several times a week and planned ultimately to retire and move back to Oregon.
